## How the score was worked out

Each result implies a score on its own, after adjusting for how hard that test is and who ran it. The model's score is their weighted average, with a small pull toward the middle for thinly tested models. Each test's weight is its *counts* column above; here it is added up by who ran the tests. [Method](../method.md)

<pre>
source                                    results  share of the score
<a name="card3-ibm-granite-granite-4-0-h-1b"></a><a href="https://huggingface.co/ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-1b/blob/d18cca4c121edb87d022116d281ce212c9136f57/README.md">ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-1b model card…</a>       21   80% ▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇

prior: pull toward the middle                        0% ▇
weighted average                                   = 40.4

## How to run it

<sub>[context source](https://huggingface.co/ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-1b/blob/d18cca4c121edb87d022116d281ce212c9136f57/README.md): Granite 4.0 Nano card architecture table (h-1b card): 'Sequence length 128K' for H 1B Dense. ollama lists a 1M context window. Observed 2026-10-10.</sub>

<pre>
download                     size  score
8-bit q8_0                 ~1.6GB   40.4
4-bit q4_k_m               ~0.9GB   40.4
4-bit mlx-4bit · mac only  ~0.8GB   40.4
4-bit mlx-8bit · mac only  ~1.6GB   40.4
</pre>

<sub>The score is the published model's; quantized downloads haven't been evaluated separately.</sub>

### Run it on your own machine

**llama.cpp** · install: macOS / Linux `curl -LsSf https://llama.app/install.sh | sh` · Windows `irm https://llama.app/install.ps1 | iex` · [other ways](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/docs/install.md) · Homebrew and winget installs name the commands llama-cli and llama-server instead.

```sh
# 4-bit q4_k_m · ~0.9GB
llama cli -hf ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-1b-GGUF:Q4_K_M
# or start a local server and open the address it prints (http://localhost:9931)
llama serve -hf ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-1b-GGUF:Q4_K_M
```

**LM Studio** · install: [macOS / Windows / Linux](https://lmstudio.ai/download) · Open the app once before using the lms command.

```sh
# 4-bit q4_k_m · ~0.9GB
lms get https://huggingface.co/ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-1b-GGUF@Q4_K_M -y
# then run lms ls to see its name, and lms chat followed by that name
# 4-bit mlx-4bit · mac only · ~0.8GB
lms get https://huggingface.co/mlx-community/granite-4.0-h-1b-4bit -y
# then run lms ls to see its name, and lms chat followed by that name
# 4-bit mlx-8bit · mac only · ~1.6GB
lms get https://huggingface.co/mlx-community/granite-4.0-h-1b-8bit -y
# then run lms ls to see its name, and lms chat followed by that name
```

**Ollama** · install: [macOS / Windows](https://ollama.com/download) · Linux `curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh`

```sh
# 8-bit q8_0 · ~1.6GB
ollama run granite4:1b-h
# 4-bit q4_k_m · ~0.9GB
ollama run hf.co/ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-1b-GGUF:Q4_K_M
```

**MLX (Mac)** · install: with uv `uv tool install mlx-lm` · or `pip install mlx-lm` · Apple silicon Macs only, text only.

```sh
# 4-bit mlx-4bit · mac only · ~0.8GB
mlx_lm.chat --model mlx-community/granite-4.0-h-1b-4bit
# or start an OpenAI-compatible server at http://localhost:8080/v1
mlx_lm.server --model mlx-community/granite-4.0-h-1b-4bit
# 4-bit mlx-8bit · mac only · ~1.6GB
mlx_lm.chat --model mlx-community/granite-4.0-h-1b-8bit
# or start an OpenAI-compatible server at http://localhost:8080/v1
mlx_lm.server --model mlx-community/granite-4.0-h-1b-8bit
```
